Brouwer fixed-point theorem.subject: Computer & IT
Brouwer fixed-point theorem.question: The _____ was Theorem in topology.
Brouwer fixed-point theorem.fact: Brouwer's fixed-point theorem is a fixed-point theorem in topology, named after L. E. J. Brouwer. It states that for any continuous function f {\displaystyle f} mapping a nonempty compact convex set to itself, there is a point x 0 {\displaystyle x_{0}} such that f ( x 0 ) = x 0 {\displaystyle f(x_{0})=x_{0}}.

Brouwer fixed-point theorem.subject: Computer & IT
Brouwer fixed-point theorem.question: A more general form than the latter is for continuous functions from a nonempty convex compact subset K {\displaystyle K} of _____ space to itself
Brouwer fixed-point theorem.fact: A more general form than the latter is for continuous functions from a nonempty convex compact subset K {\displaystyle K} of Euclidean space to itself. In its original field, this result is one of the key theorems characterizing the topology of Euclidean spaces, along with the Jordan curve theorem, the hairy ball theorem, the invariance of dimension and the Borsuk–Ulam theorem.
